thread:
emma: Heads up — a customer is seeing duplicated audit events when webhooks are enabled with S3 fallback. They see the same logical event twice in their SIEM (one from webhook, one from S3). Any known gaps?

raj: Are these real duplicates or retry attempts? We attach a retry header currently: `X-Redwood-Retry-Count` but I think payloads don't always include a stable canonical id across delivery paths.

sasha: Fwiw we added `delivery_attempt` in schema-v2 but S3 objects don't always preserve that. Suggestion: always include top-level `event_id` + `sequence_id` in the JSON body and also set them as S3 object metadata / object key. That way webhook and S3 exports carry the same canonical id. Example payload:

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01F6X9A0ZQK",
  "occurred_at": "2026-03-19T14:59:12Z",
  "type": "audit.application.update",
  "actor": {"id": "user_123", "type": "user"},
  "resource": {"id": "app_987", "type": "model"},
  "sequence_id": "seq_0001",
  "delivery_attempt": 1
}
```

auditbot: deploy: audit-schema-v2 -> prod at 2026-03-19T15:32Z :white_check_mark:

jordan: Customer's Splunk HEC ingestion was deduping by timestamp and truncation caused collisions. Recommend we document dedupe strategy: prefer `event_id` + `delivery_attempt` (and keep last N attempts) instead of relying on timestamps.

miguel: Quick note on signing: hosted webhooks currently use HMAC shared secrets (rotatable) and we add header `X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=base64(<hmac>)`. For Private we support KMS asymmetric signatures and include `X-Redwood-KMS-Key: key-id` plus `X-Redwood-Signature`. Customers asked how to verify with KMS keys. We should include a verification snippet.

sasha: Verification snippet for asymmetric KMS signatures (example):

```bash
# server has public key pubkey.pem and signature base64 in X-Redwood-Signature
echo -n '{"event_id":"evt_01F6X9A0ZQK",...}' > payload.json
base64 --decode <<< "$X_REDP_SIG" > sig.bin
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature sig.bin payload.json
```

sasha: Also add headers we will standardize: `X-Redwood-Event-Id`, `X-Redwood-Delivery-Attempt`, `X-Redwood-Signature`, `X-Redwood-KMS-Key`, and `Retry-After` on 429/5xx where applicable.

raj: Operationally: S3 fallback currently writes object key as `audit/YYYY/MM/DD/<uuid>.json`. Plan: change to `audit/YYYY/MM/DD/<event_id>-<attempt>.json` and set S3 metadata `x-amz-meta-event-id` so downstream SIEMs can dedupe by metadata instead of object name.

jordan: For Splunk/Datadog mappings: map `event_id` to `event_id` field, keep `_time` as occurred_at, and use `delivery_attempt` for ordering. Add recommended dedupe TTL doc: keep seen event_ids for 24h by default, configurable.

miguel: Question about KMS: do we want hosted customers to verify KMS signatures? We currently only publish the HMAC secret; rotating to KMS-asymmetric for hosted could break integrations. My vote: keep HMAC for hosted, asymmetric KMS for Private/air-gapped. Document differences clearly.

emma: Action items: 1) raj -> add canonical event_id into S3 object key + metadata (owner: raj, ETA: 2026-03-26) 2) sasha -> update webhook runtime to emit `X-Redwood-Event-Id` and `X-Redwood-Delivery-Attempt` headers and add header docs (owner: sasha, ETA: 2026-03-24) 3) emma -> onboarding doc + dedupe guidance for Splunk/Datadog/SIEM (owner: emma, ETA: 2026-03-27).

emma: :thumbsup: I'll draft the onboarding checklist and include sample Splunk HEC props + defaut dedupe TTL. Will ping support + solutions when draft is ready.
